places.name: The Alessian Hull

why.founding: A First-Era warship from the fleet that chased Red Bramman was lost on the reef. It settled upright in eleven metres of water.
why.siteAdvantages: The water is deep enough that the hull is intact. The stern is shallow enough for a single-breath dive.
why.occupantsMotive: Four Soulrest families dispute the ownership. The dispute has not been settled by any court.
why.pressures: Two centuries of salvage have stripped the deck. Silt fills the hold up to the coamings.
why.wouldChangeIf: One good season of settled water would let a diving team open the whole hold.

hardConstraints: on the reef line, in eight to fifteen metres of salt water
within a boat-hour of place.mercantile-coast.soulrest, on a wreck ground over which the salvage market has a live claim

places.name: Alten Meerhleel
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md (Alten Meerhleel: a port built to trade with outsiders; Hist: NONE)

why.founding: Alten Meerhleel is an outsider-facing port south-west of Lilmoth. It is below city scale. An Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. Lilmoth lay destroyed for a century and a half. During that time the bay's outside trade came to Meerhleel. Enough of that trade stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Slow deep water lies inside the bar. A laden hull can lie off in the deep water and be worked by lighters. Firm ground behind the quay carries a warehouse row. The 'alten-' in the name means outsiders.
why.occupantsMotive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports live here. The customs presence is one clerk and an unstaffed tariff shed. Traders value the port for the absence of inspection.
why.pressures: Lilmoth is rebuilt, so the two ports are now direct rivals. Meerhleel's advantage is that no questions are asked there. Corimont is the province's real free port. Questions are not asked there either. Corimont lies behind a harbour wall.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Lilmoth's council dropped its tariffs, Soulrest factors would have no reason to sail to Meerhleel. A real harbour at Lilmoth would serve their needs.

hardConstraints: sheltered navigable water off the legal lanes

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes

vibe.silhouette: A straight warehouse gable-line and two masts stand on one side of the landing. A low uneven raft-quarter with no roofline stands on the other side. The landing stage lies between them.
vibe.palette: The palette is sun-bleached deck timber, painted price boards and brown estuary water.
vibe.materials: Two kits share the landing stage. The warehouse row uses sawn plank, ridge-tile and iron strap. The raft-quarter uses lashed plank platforms on piles, with reed and cane. No frame, post or tile crosses the stage in either direction.
vibe.signatureFeature: Two building grammars stand on one waterfront. A lashed Argonian plank quarter is moored to its piles. It stands beside a straight-gabled outsiders' warehouse row. The landing stage joins the two.
vibe.condition: The port is prospering and patched. The warehouse row is maintained to the day. The raft-quarter is rebuilt continuously and looks worse for the work.
vibe.approach: From the water, the masts and a warehouse gable read together. They show before the plank quarter does.
vibe.senses: The sounds are cargo hooks, tallying and arguments in two languages. The smells are tar, bilge and unswept spice. At slack water the estuary smells brown.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest tests a port in which no questions are asked. The port's own quay has been robbed.

places.name: Ashfield

why.founding: A Colovian family founded the estate on ash-enriched lowland left by the Great Burn. The family bought out the smallholders. They put in a single plantation.
why.siteAdvantages: The ground is dry and firm. Deep burn ash lies on it. The coast road runs at the field edge.
why.occupantsMotive: The estate lacks a tenant. The house is empty. The fields have gone to scrub grass and bramble.
why.pressures: The roof timbers are failing one by one. A pack has denned under the old threshing floor.
why.wouldChangeIf: A new tenant with the coin to clear the ground could reopen the fields.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a city's agricultural hinterland

vibe.silhouette: The site is a low horizontal, the province's only open field-horizon. Scrub has made it ragged. One marker stone still stands at the road junction.
vibe.palette: Black soil is going green with weed. Dead stubble is pale. Every metal fitting has rust.
vibe.materials: The walls are rammed black earth. The wattle hurdles are rotted. Farmstead timber sags on rendered-stone footings.
vibe.signatureFeature: Roofed yard buildings stand over fields uncut for years. Charcoal still turns up in every collapsed furrow.
vibe.condition: The house range is derelict. The yard buildings are sound. Field fencing is down throughout the estate.
vibe.mood: The estate is empty and going back to scrub.
vibe.approach: The canopy still ends abruptly and sky opens above. Bramble now breaks the field lines.
vibe.senses: Wind moves through the dead stubble and bramble. A smell of char rises when a furrow is disturbed. The pack is the only thing that moves.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest is to clear the den under the threshing floor. The work must be done before the roof timbers finish failing.

localStateVariants.description: Fire has come back into the burn country and the fields are being cut as breaks.

places.name: Ashfield Hearth

why.founding: Ashfield Hearth is a village-kept fire and dry floor on the road. Villagers maintain it by rota. The coast road kills travellers who are caught out.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands where the road leaves firm ground for the salt marsh.
why.occupantsMotive: Ashfield's households keep the hearth in turn. Each guest who uses it must leave fuel.
why.pressures: Travellers routinely take fuel without leaving any. The rota is failing gradually.
why.wouldChangeIf: A season of unkept fires would end a two-hundred-year custom.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

vibe.palette: Ember orange, reed brown.
vibe.signatureFeature: The hearth is a single shuttered room. It holds a banked fire and a fuel stack. A tally board records who last filled the fuel stack.

playerPurpose.hook: A banked fire and a dry floor stand where the road leaves firm ground. Guests leave fuel. If a guest does not, the villagers remember it.

places.name: Ashroot

why.founding: Ashroot is the nearest Hist village to Soulrest. Argonian households remain in the burn country because the Hist is here.
why.siteAdvantages: The village stands on a rise that the peat fire did not cross. The tree's roots draw on water below the depth of the burn.
why.occupantsMotive: The villagers kept the tree alive through the Burn. They date the village's own history from that season.
why.pressures: The jungle edge here kills travellers who walk it alone. The villagers give this warning at the gate.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the tree would disperse the village into the city within a generation.

hardConstraints: a rise around which the peat fire passed, with root-water below it

preferences.neighbourRelation: within 2500 m of Soulrest, in the burn country behind the city

vibe.silhouette: One blue-flowered crown stands alone above a field of white dead stumps. A bright water channel rings the crown.
vibe.palette: The palette is blue blossom, black ash and green channel.
vibe.materials: Walls use mud-mother plaster and roofs use reed throughout. Wattle fire-breaks and Argonian lamp-cages stand in the village. Every post is new timber cut from outside the burn.
vibe.signatureFeature: A blue-flowered Hist stands alone in a district of dead white stumps. A low water channel rings it. The villagers dug the channel to keep fire out of the crown.
vibe.condition: The village is deliberately new. Every structure has been rebuilt since the burn. Buildings are kept clear of the dead stumps. The villagers refuse to remove the stumps.
vibe.approach: The dead stumps read first as a white field. The living crown shows only from among the stumps.
vibe.senses: Water runs in the fire channel day and night. Chime-frames sound. The scent of blossom is out of place over ash. Charcoal lies underfoot throughout the village.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest is to carry the gate warning to people who ignored it. Another is to mend the sheltering rite that is failing.

places.name: Sees-No-Root

why.founding: The village's Hist died with its mnemic egg unrecovered. The villagers organise their offices and rites around the loss.
why.siteAdvantages: The ground is unchanged and good. Villages that lose a Hist usually disperse. This village remained.
why.occupantsMotive: The villagers maintain the empty enclosure and the grave offices. They recite aloud the memories once held by the crown.
why.pressures: The children are leaving for Lilmoth. The recitation takes six days. Fewer villagers can perform it each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recovered egg would restore the village at a stroke. Treasure-hunters across Murkmire know that the reward stands.

preferences.neighbourRelation: neighbours argue about whether to admit them

vibe.silhouette: The village has a hole in its middle. A walled empty circle stands where the crown should be. The roofline dips toward it on four sides.
vibe.palette: The palette is wall moss, bare earth circle and lamp gold.
vibe.materials: Houses use mud-mother plaster and reed. One enclosure wall is of carefully laid stakes. A single hardwood recitation bench is worn to a shine.
vibe.signatureFeature: An empty walled tree-enclosure faces a worn smooth recitation bench. Every evening a villager speaks the whole village's memory to a stump-socket.
vibe.condition: The village is well kept. The villagers maintain the empty enclosure more carefully than any house.
vibe.approach: The village looks ordinary from every direction. Inside the ring of houses, the enclosure that the houses face becomes visible.
vibe.senses: One voice recites at the same hour each evening. The rest of the village stays quiet for the recitation. The enclosure wall has wet moss. The root-hum is absent from the village.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest is to find speakers for the recitation. Another is to find the mnemic egg around which the village organised its life.

places.name: Murkmire Pulled Field

why.founding: The grave-poles of a burial ground were pulled out by persons unknown. The bog blight came up afterwards.
why.siteAdvantages: The site is an old village burial ground on soft peat. Soft peat is the condition that the blight requires.
why.occupantsMotive: The field belongs to no household. The blight keeps to the field. The villagers fenced the field by common consent.
why.pressures: The pulled poles lie where they were dropped. The grave-warden cannot match each pole to its grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: Driving the poles back in the right order would end the blight. A grave-singer must enter the field to do it.

vibe.approach: A fenced wattle boundary has pahnjees hung on it. Beyond the boundary, peat gives under the boot.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest is to drive the pulled poles back in the order set down by the register. The field is awake on every side.

playerPurpose.hook: The field is a grave-field with half its poles pulled. The ground still shifts.

places.name: The Carrying House

why.founding: Argonians who die in stone prisons can still return if their bones are brought to the dirt. A halfway house for the bones had to be built.
why.siteAdvantages: The house stands on the burn-country track between White Rose and the coast road. It is one day's carry from either.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers rest, re-wrap and re-label bundles here. The keeper records every name that passes through the house and where it is going.
why.pressures: The register is longer than the number of bodies that have actually reached a Hist.
why.wouldChangeIf: If White Rose were emptied, the house would become a memorial. It would cease to be a service.

hardConstraints: on a walked or poled route

preferences.neighbourRelation: between a carceral site and the interior

places.name: Bramman's Screen

why.founding: The site is the seaward mouth, in dense mangrove, of a narrow winding river. Red Bramman escaped the Alessian navy by that river.
why.siteAdvantages: Four channel mouths open off the same bay. This one carries water at the top of the tide for about ninety minutes.
why.occupantsMotive: The pilots who know the run sell the knowledge. A wrong channel strands a hull until the next tide.
why.pressures: The route is worth something only while it stays unmarked. A scheduled ferry service on the route would end that.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt pulse could close the channel or open a second. Either change would end the pilots' monopoly.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water

preferences.neighbourRelation: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

notableNpcSlots.role: screen pilot who sells the ninety minutes

vibe.silhouette: The site has no silhouette. Four identical black mangrove mouths stand in an unbroken wall of root. They are indistinguishable until the water drops.
vibe.palette: The palette is black water, root brown and green tunnel light.
vibe.materials: The materials are living mangrove root, a sand sill, one cut tide-mark and a few unpainted marker withies. One stake platform inside the true channel is the built work here.
vibe.signatureFeature: Four identical mangrove mouths open off the bay. One of them is false-bottomed with a sand sill. A tide-mark is cut into a root. The tide-mark is legible only at slack water.
vibe.condition: The site is untouched by design. A built marker would advertise the channel.
vibe.approach: From the bay the site looks like solid mangrove until the tide reaches the right point. Then one mouth is darker than the others.
vibe.senses: Water sucks through the roots at the turn of the tide. Insects sound and no human sound is heard. At the mouth of the right channel the smell changes from salt to tannin.

questHooks.opportunity: A quest is to run the navigable mouth inside its ninety minutes. Another is to prevent the channel being marked.

places.name: Bright-Throat Village

why.founding: The Bright-Throat tribe brokers alliances between tribes and works fine crafts. The village stands on the mangrove wall above Oliis Bay. The tribe has brokered the settlements that followed each of the region's catastrophes.
why.siteAdvantages: The village is a platform village that stands clear of the tide on the mangrove wall. One stair leads down to a beach landing. The whole approach to Lilmoth can be seen from the dry and defensible site.
why.occupantsMotive: The villagers pursue diplomacy and craft. Other tribes come to Bright-Throat because of its Listening-Tree and its chimes. The Bright-Throat tribe does not go to the other tribes.
why.pressures: Every trading party on Oliis Bay wants Bright-Throat's endorsement. Keeping neutral is expensive for the tribe.
why.wouldChangeIf: Taking a side in the Lilmoth–An-Xileel quarrel would cost the tribe its role as broker. The tribe is known for that role.

hardConstraints: on the mangrove wall above a beach landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: commands the bay approach to Lilmoth; one stair to the water

vibe.silhouette: Long lashed platforms stand on mangrove trunks and rise in three levels up the wall. Dyed cloth hangs on every rail. One stair goes down to the sand.
vibe.palette: The rock is warm ochre. The chime frames are painted. The bay below is blue.
vibe.materials: The houses are built of shack-kit plank and cane and stand on a dry rock bench with no stilts and no mud. The rock shelf is the floor and the walkways are lashed. Bone and tin hang from the painted hardwood chime frames.
vibe.signatureFeature: Houses stand on a cliff bench. Tuned bone and tin chimes hang from the houses. The chimes can be heard over the water well before the houses are visible.
vibe.condition: The village is dry, sound and comfortable. Little rots on the bench. The carpentry is the best work in Murkmire.
vibe.approach: From the water the stair is seen first, then the platforms above it. From inland the top deck is underfoot before the village is seen.
vibe.senses: Tuned chimes can be heard half a mile over water. Wind blows off the bay. The dry rock stays warm. Cooking smoke rises in a straight line.

questHooks.opportunity: An endorsement from Bright-Throat can be bought, earned or exposed. The whole bay treats Bright-Throat as neutral.

places.name: The Ash Cairns

why.founding: The dead of the western end of the Great Burn lie in the cairns. They lie where they were found. There were too many dead to carry.
why.siteAdvantages: The site is a rise at the edge of the ash plain. It was the first ground that did not burn.
why.occupantsMotive: Grave-singers still come to the cairns. They keep the count and recite it. The count is not a round number.
why.pressures: Poles will not stand in ash. The dead here are marked in stone. The mourners who come resent the compromise.
why.wouldChangeIf: The place does not change. That is the purpose of the cairns.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

vibe.palette: The stone is grey. The ash is white. One tree is green.
vibe.signatureFeature: Two hundred low stone cairns stand in rows on the edge of an ash plain. Each cairn has a plain grave-pole laid flat across it. The poles are not driven into the ground.

places.name: The Overpass

why.founding: The roots and branches of two great trees meet forty feet above a channel. The channel is too dangerous to swim. The crossing was obvious to the villagers.
why.siteAdvantages: The canopy touches across the channel here. Six kilometres separate this crossing from the next such crossing.
why.occupantsMotive: The villages on both banks maintain the crossing. They renew the lashings every dry season.
why.pressures: The channel below is home to the crocodile stock. The crocodiles make the crossing necessary.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing either tree would end the crossing. Every journey between the banks would then take a day longer.

vibe.palette: The canopy is green. The lashing is pale. The water below is dark.
vibe.signatureFeature: A living root-and-branch bridge has lashed handlines. It stands forty feet above the water. Crocodiles are visible in the water.
vibe.mood: The crossing is exhilarating. The people who live here find it routine.

playerPurpose.hook: A living root bridge stands forty feet over water that crocodiles occupy. The alternative to the bridge is swimming.

places.name: Chasepoint

why.founding: Chasepoint is an Imperial road stage that the Legion built. The wreck-salvage families of the coast keep the stage now. Soulrest is the nearest town, a short walk away. Lore names Chasepoint as the neighbour east of Soulrest.
why.siteAdvantages: Chasepoint stands on the last firm ground before the coast road turns inland. The sea lies to the south, out of sight of the stage. Wreckage from the Southern Sea comes ashore on the coast to the south.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage rights at Chasepoint are hereditary. The families guard these rights closely. They dry recovered rope and cordage in the stage's old stable.
why.pressures: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries. Two families each claim the keeper's office. The roof is Argonian reed thatch on Imperial walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A revived coast road with paid stage-keepers would make Chasepoint a proper town again.

preferences.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing along a road

notableNpcSlots.role: station-keeper who holds an inherited Imperial office

vibe.silhouette: The Imperial way-station has a straight ridge and an Argonian reed roof. A square yard wall stands beside it.
vibe.palette: The palette is grey plaster, rubble stone and bleached driftwood.
vibe.materials: The walls are Imperial grey plaster over a rubble core. Argonian reed thatch covers them. The families call the thatched roof a bodge. The yard stacks are ships' timber cut in other provinces.
vibe.signatureFeature: An Imperial way-station has an Argonian reed roof. Its yard holds stacks of ships' timber cut in other provinces.
vibe.condition: The stage is sound but scavenged. The pantiles are gone. The families replaced the roof with local reed. The rest of the building is Imperial and holds.

places.name: The Hereguard Terraces

why.pressures: A single tenant who takes water out of turn ruins a terrace three levels down.

places.name: Hereguard Plantation

why.siteAdvantages: The estate stands on a river terrace that floods every year. The flood ruins any other crop and suits rice.
why.occupantsMotive: A Breton family and Argonian tenant households live here. A share arrangement binds them. Both sides describe the arrangement differently.
why.pressures: Lilmoth depends on Hereguard rice. That dependence gives the tenants more hold over the family every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tenant refusal at planting would starve the city. Both sides have made that calculation.

hardConstraints: a river terrace that floods seasonally, with slack water at its foot

preferences.neighbourRelation: holds the crossing that its neighbours must use

vibe.materials: The house uses Breton dressed stone and slate. The terrace bunds are packed clay and stone. The worker village uses Argonian reed and cane. The house and the worker village stand three hundred metres apart. They share no wall or well.

why.siteAdvantages: The village stands on a defensible rise with a single approach. The rise is three days from Lilmoth. Water does not reach the rise.
why.occupantsMotive: A Blackguards band moved into the burn scar. The village had chosen the rise for its single watchable approach.
why.pressures: The lookouts of the gang watch the same path as the old boundary speakers.
why.wouldChangeIf: Driving the gang out would reopen the shortest route across the jungle belt. The village itself once blocked that route.

places.name: The Sakka Fall

why.occupantsMotive: The chamber has no residents between visits. Visitors have used it as a shrine, a cache and a hiding place, in that order. Visitors will probably use it as a hiding place again.
why.pressures: The chamber floods when the river rises. People most want to hide in the chamber when the river is high.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the river's course changed, the chamber would empty and be exposed.

places.name: Sakka Head

why.founding: Sakka Head is the furthest point that a loaded canoe can reach up the Keel-Sakka. A loaded canoe reaches it only in the wet season. In the dry season the head of navigation is two kilometres downstream.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock sill is a rapid in the wet season and a dry step in the dry season. A level bank beside the sill is used for stacking cargo.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters take over cargo handling at Sakka Head. The porters' season depends on where the head of navigation lies each month.
why.pressures: The head of navigation moves, so the porters rebuild the porter yard twice a year. The porters refuse to build in stone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the sill would push navigation four kilometres further upriver. That change would destroy the porters' trade.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

why.pressures: The chime-relay of Bright-Throat reaches the landing. The writ of Lilmoth does not reach the landing. The families of the landing prefer this.

places.name: Black Fin Grove

why.occupantsMotive: Four villages keep the grove by rota. Each of the four villages claims the grove as its own.
why.pressures: The story of Keshu has four incompatible versions. The villages keep the rota so that they never have to settle which version is true.

why.occupantsMotive: The households live rent-free in sight of the city. The mooring fee is a fraction of the cost of a shore plot.

why.wouldChangeIf: A legal definition of a mooring as a dwelling would end the settlement.

places.name: Lilmoth

why.founding: The Slaughter of 4E 48 destroyed the old city of Lilmoth. Argonians rebuilt Lilmoth after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast. The rebuilt city is smaller and lower than the city that it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: Lilmoth stands on firm ground at the head of the estuary, with shallow water about 128 m from its centre. The lighter quay runs out into the shallows. Big ships anchor out in Oliis Bay and lightermen bring their cargo ashore by lighter, a trade that supports the city.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs Lilmoth by tariff. The council refuses to appoint a ruler, because the last faction to hold sole power destroyed the city.
why.pressures: Lilmoth is hostile to the An-Xileel successor state. The merchants of the bay must trade through Lilmoth. The city stands over the mass grave of the drowned Imperial city.
why.wouldChangeIf: Lilmoth has its own Hist tree, the third Hist. If the third Hist spoke to one faction alone, every institution in Lilmoth would fail. The world rules forbid the third Hist from favouring one faction.

hardConstraints: Firm shelf at the head of the estuary, with the lighter quay running out into shallow tidal water

preferences.densityGradient: city core; the densest civil gradient in the south

why.founding: The Drake Hole is a drowned sinkhole in the bay floor. The sinkhole is forty metres deep. A creature lives at the bottom of it.
why.siteAdvantages: The hole is deep, cold and permanent. The rest of the bay is shallow.
why.occupantsMotive: The creature in the hole holds the attention of the fishers. The fishers work around the hole in a circle. The circle shows on any chart of their nets.
why.pressures: The hole lies directly on the natural lighterage line. Every hull on that line crosses the hole.
why.wouldChangeIf: Bay crews will not attempt the hole.

hardConstraints: deep standing salt water over a bay floor
off the Oliis bay, within a morning's paddle of Breathing-Stone

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a boat lane, so the bay traffic passes over it

vibe.palette: The colours are blue-black, a cold green rim and a silver bait shoal.
vibe.signatureFeature: A circle of open water has no net set across it. A visible temperature line marks the rim of the circle. Beneath this circle lie forty metres of black water.

places.deferredWhy: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. That rebalance has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-3 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.

playerPurpose.hook: A hole forty metres deep lies in the bay floor. The fishers do not name the hole at sea. A creature lives in the hole.

loot.provenance: what the hole has taken off the lane above it

places.name: Estuary Stage

why.founding: The estuary is half a mile wide at the road crossing. The ferry is older than the rebuilt city.
why.siteAdvantages: The crossing is a narrows with hard landings on both sides. Slack water comes twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: The council grants the ferry as a concession, farmed out annually to the highest bidder. The winning bidder sets the fare.
why.pressures: The fare rises every year. The boats do not improve.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rival free crossing upstream would break the concession. The council would then lose its revenue from the concession.

hardConstraints: at a water narrows the coast road must cross

preferences.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

vibe.silhouette: Two hard landings face each other across brown water. A fare board on a post is the tallest thing in sight.
vibe.palette: The colours are painted board red, brown estuary and grey plank.
vibe.materials: The landing ramps are stone-faced. The ferry is a plank swim-ferry. Rowboats also serve the crossing. Market tents stand on the waiting side. The fare board is painted plank that has been repainted five times.
vibe.signatureFeature: A wide flat ferry carries a painted fare board. The board has been repainted over five times, each time higher.
vibe.condition: The landings and the ferry are maintained. The rest of the place is only tolerated.
vibe.approach: The road ends at the water. The fare board is read before the ferry is in sight.
vibe.senses: Waiting travellers make queue noise. Guar stand among the queue. The ferry is worked with a sweep-oar. An argument breaks out at the fare board on most crossings.

localGroups.name: Estuary Ferry Holders
localGroups.reason: Ferry holders are boat crews on a route.

playerPurpose.hook: The crossing saves a two-day walk round the estuary.

terrainRequests.note: The estuary must pinch at the crossing, or the ferry has no landing mark.
The estuary must pinch here, or the coast road has no crossing to be farmed out.

places.name: Oliis Pull

why.founding: Oliis Pull is where the whole ebb of the estuary squeezes past a rock spur. The current runs four knots for three hours at a stretch.
why.siteAdvantages: The narrows cannot be avoided on the river route. The alternative is a day's portage.
why.occupantsMotive: Oliis Pull is uninhabited. Boat crews wait on the tide to pass it.
why.pressures: Loaded canoes are lost here every year. Boat crews treat the loss as weather.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the spur back would halve the current. The cut would cost more than the province has.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a boat lane; forces a portage or a wait

vibe.palette: The colours are a brown-white race, black rock and a bare mud beach.
vibe.signatureFeature: A standing wave forms off a black rock spur. A waiting beach lies on the upstream side. Generations of boat crews sitting out the ebb have worn the beach bare.

places.deferredWhy: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'drowning-narrows' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

playerPurpose.hook: The current runs four knots past a black spur for three hours at a time. A boat crew can wait it out on the beach or take it loaded.

places.name: The Cut Reef

why.founding: The Cut Reef is harvested for lime, lacquer shell and building aggregate. It is not harvested for pearl. The stilts of Lilmoth need footings.
why.siteAdvantages: The reef is shallow enough to work by free-diving. It is close enough to barge the take straight to the city.
why.occupantsMotive: Cutters take from the reef by permit from the council. Lilmoth licenses no other harvest in the bay.
why.pressures: The reef is visibly smaller than it was in living memory. The permit count of the council has not fallen.
why.wouldChangeIf: Closing the reef would raise the cost of every new platform in Lilmoth.

hardConstraints: clear water over a worked bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: worked from Lilmoth’s quay; within 2 km of the city, on the bay’s inner reef

vibe.palette: The colours are bleached coral white, blue water and a grey barge.
vibe.signatureFeature: The reef is cut into steps like a quarry. Barge moorings lie over the deepest workings. A permit board stands on a post.

questHooks.opportunity: A diver can dive the worked steps that the cutters have abandoned.

places.deferredWhy: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. That rebalance has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-4 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.

playerPurpose.hook: The stilts of Lilmoth stand on lime cut from this reef. The cutters are short of divers.

loot.provenance: cut lime, lacquer shell and aggregate, stacked on the raft

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 5 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Half-Day Flat is two miles of Oliis Bay flat. Travellers can walk it at low water and must sail it at high water. The difference between the two is ninety minutes.
why.siteAdvantages: The flat cuts hours off the coast route for a crew that reads the tide correctly. How much flat the ebb uncovers depends on the tidal amplitude of Oliis Bay. The uncovered distance is not fixed.
why.occupantsMotive: Local carriers use the flat daily. Strangers use it once.
why.pressures: The tide reaches the flat from the rear. The tide moves faster than a person walks.
why.wouldChangeIf: A marked causeway would make the flat safe. A marked causeway would also remove the reason to read the tide.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water

preferences.neighbourRelation: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

vibe.silhouette: The horizon is flat and made of whatever the ebb uncovers. A line of leaning withies crosses the flat. A bell post stands at each end.
vibe.palette: The colours are silver mud, grey sky and dark withy.
vibe.materials: The materials are mud and withy. The built work is two bell posts and the marker line. The footprint of the route is whatever the tide uncovers.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tide uncovers the flat. Withies mark the flat and lean toward the source of the flood. A bell post at each end stops ringing when the water turns.
vibe.condition: The flat cannot bear any building, so it stays unbuilt. Carriers replace the withies after every spring tide.
vibe.approach: The flat opens out with the far bell post at the edge of vision. The near bell is already ringing.
vibe.senses: A bell at each end stops when the flood starts. Oystercatchers call over the flat. The flat makes a sucking sound underfoot. The wind is unbroken.

localStateVariants.description: The flat is walkable and the bells are ringing.
Sailable water; the withies lean and the bells are silent.

playerPurpose.hook: A traveller who reads the tide right saves half a day. A traveller who reads it wrong is stranded two miles out on a flooding flat.

loot.provenance: what the flat keeps of people who mistimed it

places.name: The Anchored Wreck

why.founding: The Anchored Wreck is a deep-water trader. It dragged its anchor in a blow and drove onto the bay flats. It still stands upright.
why.siteAdvantages: The wreck is grounded upright in two metres of water. It is visible across the whole anchorage.
why.occupantsMotive: Lighter crews use the wreck as a marker. They also use it as a smoking shelter. The cargo went in the first week.
why.pressures: The wreck lies directly on the lighterage line. It settles further into the path of the lighter crews every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Breaking up the wreck would clear the line. Breaking it up would cost more than the council will pay.

hardConstraints: aground on a tidal flat, dry at low water

preferences.neighbourRelation: inside sight of the Oliis bay traffic; walkable from the flat at low tide

vibe.palette: The colours are tarred hull black, grey mud and bright washing.
vibe.signatureFeature: A full-rigged trading hull stands upright on a mudflat. Its masts are still up. Washing lines are rigged between the masts.
vibe.approach: The wreck is visible from every part of Oliis Bay.

places.deferredWhy: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'wreck' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

playerPurpose.hook: A trader stands upright on the bay flats. It can be boarded on foot at low water.

loot.provenance: cargo nobody has been able to claim without admitting how it got there

places.name: The Ledger Camp

why.founding: Households were turned off their ground for owed labour. They camped at the edge of the ground. Leaving would forfeit their claim entirely.
why.siteAdvantages: The camp is on the boundary of the estate that evicted the households. It is in sight of their own fields.
why.occupantsMotive: Staying is how the households keep their claim. Every day in the camp presses the argument.
why.pressures: The ledger house says the debt grows while the households camp. The households say the debt does not grow. The original ledger entry is illegible.
why.wouldChangeIf: Producing the original ledger page would settle the dispute one way or the other.

preferences.neighbourRelation: immediately outside an estate village

vibe.palette: The colours are mud, salvaged thatch and green crop that extends beyond the shore.
vibe.signatureFeature: The camp is laid out along a field boundary. The evicted households carried their door-posts from their old houses. They re-erected the door-posts facing the fields.

places.deferredWhy: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'owing-eviction-camp' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

playerPurpose.hook: Households camp on the boundary of the ground from which they were evicted. Leaving would forfeit their claim.

places.name: Turns-The-Pilgrims

why.founding: Turns-The-Pilgrims is the last rest on the pilgrim route to the Teeth of Sithis. Nisswo of the Turning Path keeps the house.
why.siteAdvantages: The house is a day short of the temple. It stands on the only firm ground on the final approach.
why.occupantsMotive: The house keepers house pilgrims free. They preach the decay-sermon at the pilgrims. Most pilgrims come for the sermon.
why.pressures: A rival reading of the sermon is preached three days back down the route.
why.wouldChangeIf: A schism would split the route. A schism would split the house with it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: between villages on a preaching circuit

vibe.palette: The colours are rotting timber, lamp gold and black water.
vibe.signatureFeature: The walls of the rest house are deliberately unrepaired. The decay of each year is marked and dated as part of the teaching.

places.deferredWhy: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'nisswo-rest-house' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

playerPurpose.hook: The house offers the last bed before the Teeth of Sithis. The bed is free. The decay-sermon is included.

places.name: Xal-Meht

why.founding: Xal-Meht is a xanmeer with no surviving clan. Pilgrims on the way to the Teeth of Sithis tend it.
why.siteAdvantages: The xanmeer stands on the pilgrim line. A spring flows at its foot. The spring is why the route goes this way.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims treat maintenance as devotion. Each party clears one terrace before continuing along the route.
why.pressures: Pilgrim tending is uneven. The unloved terraces are being lost.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rerouted pilgrimage would leave the xanmeer to the forest within thirty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it

notableNpcSlots.role: Sweeper who decides what the path can see

vibe.silhouette: The monument is stepped. One edge is hard and swept and the other is soft and green. The swept side is the side that the path overlooks.
vibe.palette: The colours are grey stone, moss green and pilgrim cloth colour.
vibe.materials: The monument is xanmeer stone with ornament courses. Moss is left standing on three faces. Pilgrim cloth is tied to the stair rails. No additions are bonded to the stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The stepped monument is half swept and half green. The swept terraces are those visible from the path.
vibe.condition: The pilgrims keep half the monument maintained on purpose. The line between the halves has not moved in living memory.
vibe.approach: The monument breaks the canopy line from the pilgrim path. It is one of the few reliable landmarks in Murkmire.
vibe.senses: Spring water runs at the foot. Pilgrims sweep. Cloth moves in the wind. The swept side is hot dry stone. Cold wet stone lies six feet away.

playerPurpose.hook: The xanmeer has no clan left. Passing pilgrims keep it open. The lower rooms are not kept.

loot.provenance: pilgrim offerings, left where the clan’s would have gone
the untended lower chambers

places.name: The Outside Barge

why.founding: Pusbottom's gaming tables moved onto the water when the council had started raiding buildings. The tables have stayed afloat since.
why.siteAdvantages: The barge is moored outside the wall line and is reachable only by boat. The barge can shift berth in an hour.
why.occupantsMotive: The barge's business is dice, obligation-broking and buying debts.
why.pressures: The council knows precisely where the barge is. The council moves against it only when a council member loses badly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A licensed gaming house inside the wall would close the barge. No councillor gains by proposing a licensed house.

hardConstraints: a mooring is half the type
moored off Lilmoth's sunken quarter, on the water side of the stilts, reachable without entering the city

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

vibe.signatureFeature: The barge is lantern-lit and a shallow-draught tender is kept alongside. A bell warns the tables.
vibe.mood: The mood is cheerful. The terms the barge offers are predatory.

places.name: Quin'rawl Anchorage

why.founding: Southern Sea crews anchor here, many of them Khajiit. The crews keep out of sight of Altmer and Maormer warships. No state looks at this cove.
why.siteAdvantages: The cove is a deep lagoon behind a headland and has two ways out. The bottom is sand holding ground. A freshwater run enters at the head of the cove.
why.occupantsMotive: Half the hulls carry a Soulrest charter. All the hulls carry cargo that the charter does not mention.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council both licenses and disowns the crews. The arrangement is stable. The captains resent it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A Dominion sweep of the Southern Sea would scatter the anchorage to the mangroves in a week.

hardConstraints: a deep lagoon cove behind a headland, with a second way out to the sea

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a shipping lane it can reach and leave

notableNpcSlots.role: chartered ship's master whom the other crews pretend not to know

vibe.silhouette: Six low mastless hull-lines lie in a cove under a dark headland. One properly rigged ship is anchored in the middle of them. The rigged ship looks entirely respectable.
vibe.palette: The colours are sailcloth ochre, wet sand and dark cliff green.
vibe.materials: The shore camp is sailcloth. Beached hulls serve as stores. Scaffold cargo-shears stand on the beach. Every structure on the beach is temporary.
vibe.signatureFeature: Six low hulls are moored bow-and-stern in the cove. A shore camp of sailcloth stands on the beach. A chartered ship is anchored among the hulls.
vibe.condition: The anchorage is a camp. The whole camp can be off the beach in three hours.
vibe.approach: Neither entrance shows the anchorage until the headland is passed. Past the headland the whole cove is in view at once.
vibe.senses: The cove has rigging in the headland wind, dogs, roasting meat and tar. Fresh water runs at the head of the cove.

questHooks.opportunity: The licence-and-denial arrangement can be put in writing. It can be written for one side or the other.

playerPurpose.hook: Crews who keep clear of two navies anchor here. The crews trade off the beach.

loot.provenance: cargo landed here rather than at any quay

places.name: Rockpark

why.founding: Pestilence, plague and a curse emptied Rockpark of every business and guild. No household returned. Rockpark's Hist died.
why.siteAdvantages: Rockpark stands on good firm ground. It lies on the upland road north-west out of Lilmoth.
why.occupantsMotive: Rockpark is empty. The Unearthed Equipment Store still blocks the palace gate. The palace still holds what the royal family became.
why.pressures: Rockpark is a day's walk from a living city. It is stocked with five centuries of untouched goods. The taboo against entering holds.
why.wouldChangeIf: A confirmed cure for whatever is in the palace would strip the town in a week.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it

vibe.silhouette: The town skyline is complete and has no smoke in it. Every roof stands and every chimney is cold. One collapsed store is jammed diagonally across the palace gate.
vibe.palette: The colours are dust grey, faded shop-paint and black doorways.
vibe.materials: The buildings are made of mud-mother plaster, bamboo frame, shack-kit and wattle. All the materials are five centuries weathered. No rebuilding has occurred in the village. The shop paint is original.
vibe.signatureFeature: The whole town has its shop shutters closed. The stock is still on the shelves. A collapsed equipment store is jammed across the palace gate.
vibe.condition: Intact and unlooted.
vibe.approach: The road runs straight into the town. The road carries no mark of warning.
vibe.senses: The town is absolutely silent. Dust hangs in the air and doors move in the wind. The streets are empty of birds.

questHooks.opportunity: The plague town can be entered while stocked with five centuries of goods. Deeds to the goods are already being sold.

localStateVariants.description: A thief has broken the taboo. The shelves are stripped. The district knows who did it.

places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 768 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

playerPurpose.hook: Plague emptied Rockpark and no household came back. The houses were left furnished.

loot.provenance: households locked at the plague and still shut
the guild books that record the last month

places.name: The Rockpark Stump

why.founding: Rockpark was never resettled because its Hist died. The Hist held the memory that the village kept in it.
why.siteAdvantages: The stump stands in the town's central enclosure, which is still walled. Pilgrims still sweep it. The pilgrims come and do not stay.
why.occupantsMotive: The enclosure is uninhabited. Tree-minders from three villages visit annually. They take no cutting.
why.pressures: A dead Hist's mnemic egg is a theological emergency. The region's tree-minders keep passing the problem between them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cutting taking root here would change Murkmire's whole map of who is owed what.

preferences.neighbourRelation: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

vibe.palette: The colours are ash-grey wood, green wall moss and bright offering cloth.
vibe.signatureFeature: A hollow grey stump stands inside a maintained wall. Visitors place offerings on its rim. The visitors then leave immediately.

places.deferredWhy: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'harmed-hist' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

playerPurpose.hook: A hollow grey stump stands inside a swept wall. Three villages each send a tree-minder once a year.

places.name: Under-Root

why.founding: The gallery is a walkable passage under a great root mass. It stays dry above the flood. People who wanted somewhere out of sight have occupied it for as long as the villages remember.
why.siteAdvantages: The gallery is two hundred metres of natural passage. It has three entrances and a permanent air flow.
why.occupantsMotive: Whoever is currently in the gallery occupies it. The tenancy changes, but the fittings do not.
why.pressures: The gallery floods to chest height in the deep wet season. The flood comes on about a week's notice.
why.wouldChangeIf: A root collapse would close the middle of the gallery. The collapse would split it into two dead ends.

hardConstraints: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded

preferences.neighbourRelation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map

vibe.silhouette: A living tunnel mouth opens at the base of a root buttress. Warm air flows from the mouth. Three worn approaches converge on it.
vibe.palette: The colours are root brown, soot black and green entrance light.
vibe.materials: Living root forms the wall, floor and ceiling. Three tenancies cut niches and hearth-scars at three heights. Lamp brackets are driven into wood, never stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tunnel is living root. Three tenancies cut hearth-scars and shelf niches into it at three different heights.
vibe.condition: People have reoccupied the gallery continuously for centuries. Each tenancy's alterations cut across the last one's.
vibe.mood: The place is sheltered. It belongs to another owner.
vibe.approach: Warm air is felt on the path before the mouth comes into view.
vibe.senses: A permanent through-draught is warm at one end and cold at the other. The gallery smells of soot and sap. The root hums under bare feet.

questHooks.opportunity: A tenant is living in the gallery. The tenant can be reached before the wet season fills it.

playerPurpose.hook: The gallery is two hundred metres of dry passage under the roots. A tenant is living in it.

loot.provenance: goods held between a landing and a buyer

places.name: Customs Suburb

why.founding: The suburb was the Imperial customs suburb outside Lilmoth's north gate. The An-Xileel looted it when they took the city from the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: The suburb stands astride the north road. Every cargo had to pass along that road.
why.occupantsMotive: The suburb is unrebuilt. Lilmoth's rebuilt council collects at the quay. The council prefers not to be reminded of the suburb.
why.pressures: The suburb's record room survived the fire. The records have not been read in two centuries.
why.wouldChangeIf: The records would establish who owned what before 4E 48. Several families would prefer that this stayed unknown.

hardConstraints: in a port or a city
on the road out of Lilmoth’s north gate, at the gate itself

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a living settlement that does not talk about it

vibe.silhouette: A street of roofless Imperial gables runs ahead. The road still runs dead straight through them. One vaulted roof still stands at the end of the street.
vibe.palette: The colours are fire-black render, red brick core and green regrowth.
vibe.materials: The walls are fire-blacked render over a red brick core. Fallen pantile and iron window grilles remain. Every material is Imperial.
vibe.signatureFeature: A burnt street of Imperial offices has the road still running through it. One vaulted record room still has its roof.
vibe.condition: The suburb is burnt and left. It is structurally dangerous and unrepaired. Two centuries of green growth are established inside every room.
vibe.approach: The north road runs straight down the middle of the suburb. The record room's roof is the only roof that reads as whole.
vibe.senses: Wind blows through open windows. Regrowth cracks the render. A wet ash smell remains in the render. Road noise comes from beyond the suburb.

questHooks.opportunity: The surviving record room can be read. Pages are being written into the record room.

playerPurpose.hook: The Empire's customs quarter was looted in a night and never cleared. The cellars are still sealed.

loot.provenance: duty taken on the last day the Empire held the gate
the seizure books, which name families still trading

places.name: The Drying House

why.founding: Lilmoth's sap trade produced many people who could not stop using sap. The villages built the house to put them somewhere.
why.siteAdvantages: The house stands outside the city and upwind, with running water beside it. No sap is within a day's walk in any direction.
why.occupantsMotive: Former sap users run the house. The treatment is time, water and work. No supply of sap is allowed in the house.
why.pressures: The city's dealers know precisely where the house is. One dealer funds the house. The keepers argue about the funding and take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Closing the illicit taps in the jungle would empty the house in five years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: just outside a settlement, near sap country

vibe.palette: The colours are whitewash, rope hemp and running water.
vibe.signatureFeature: A long dormitory hall has barred windows facing away from the city. A work yard of rope-making never stops.

places.deferredWhy: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
